subject: Critical Thinking
title: Predicate Logic: Beyond Simple Statements
description: A 60-second lesson on Predicate Logic: Beyond Simple Statements.

hook.text: 'All dogs are loyal' can't be expressed in propositional logic. You need something more powerful.

buildup.text: Predicate logic adds quantifiers: ∀ (for all) and ∃ (there exists). Now you can talk about categories.

discovery.text: ∀x(Dog(x) → Loyal(x)) means 'For all x, if x is a dog, then x is loyal.' Precise and testable.

twist.text: Gottlob Frege invented it in 1879. It was so advanced that almost nobody understood it for 20 years.

climax.text: Predicate logic became the foundation of computer databases, AI reasoning engines, and legal formalization.

punchline.text: To reason about the world, you need to quantify it.

quiz.question: What does the ∀ symbol mean in predicate logic?

details.summary: Predicate logic extends propositional logic by analyzing the internal structure of statements using quantifiers (all, some) and predicates. It can express relationships and generalizations that propositional logic cannot capture.
details.whyItMatters: Predicate logic is essential for mathematics, computer science, and any reasoning that involves generalizations about classes of objects.
takeaways: Predicate logic adds quantifiers: universal and existential
It captures relationships between objects, not just truth values
It is more expressive but more complex than propositional logic

faq.question: What can predicate logic express that propositional logic cannot?
faq.answer: Statements like 'All dogs are mammals' and 'Some students passed the exam' require quantifiers over objects, which propositional logic treats as unanalyzable wholes.

faq.question: What are the two main quantifiers in predicate logic?
faq.answer: The universal quantifier (for all) asserts something about every object in a domain, and the existential quantifier (there exists) asserts something about at least one object.
